scenes.title: Earth's Shifting Skin
scenes.narration: Our planet's outer shell isn't solid; it's a mosaic of about 15 major tectonic plates, moving a few centimeters each year—roughly the same speed your fingernails grow!

scenes.title: Driven by Mantle Convection
scenes.narration: The plates float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere, propelled by powerful convection currents in the mantle, where hot material rises and cooler material sinks, much like boiling water.

scenes.title: Three Boundary Types
scenes.narration: Plates interact at three main boundaries: divergent (pulling apart), convergent (colliding), and transform (sliding past), each generating distinct geological features.

scenes.title: The Pacific Ring of Fire
scenes.narration: A prime example is the Pacific Ring of Fire, where numerous convergent plate boundaries create 75% of the world's volcanoes and 90% of its earthquakes.

scenes.title: Shaping Continents & Oceans
scenes.narration: Plate tectonics continuously reshapes our planet, forming mountains, opening ocean basins, and causing continents to drift, profoundly influencing Earth's climate and biodiversity over geological timescales.
